One year after the death of its founder, Akinloye Tofowomo, popularly known as Akiin Shuga, premium live music ensemble, Shuga Band, has unveiled a new brand identity in honour of the late musician and to strengthen his legacy. The band dedicated October to celebrating its founder, who died on October 30, 2025. It unveiled a redesigned logo across its media platforms and showcased the new identity at its engagements throughout the month. The new logo features an image of Akiin Shuga holding a microphone, reflecting his lifelong dedication to music and entertainment. As part of the commemorative activities, the band also released Best of Akiin Shuga, a compilation of the late musician’s live performances, on digital platforms. Add us to your Preferred Sources According to the band, the initiatives are part of efforts to preserve its founder’s legacy while strengthening its structure in the post-founder era. Established in 1998, Shuga Band has built a reputation as one of Nigeria’s longest-serving live music ensembles, entertaining audiences at exclusive social and corporate events for more than two decades. In its efforts to sustain the business, the band had earlier unveiled a Valentine medley and announced the constitution of an advisory board comprising industry professionals to provide oversight and strategic direction. Shuga Band continues Akiin Shuga’s legacy with Valentine classics Popular live-band leader, Akiin Shuga, dies at 50 Despite the loss of its founder, the ensemble has continued to secure engagements at major events, including the 60th birthday celebration of Dr Muiz Banire, Seplat Nigerian Content Day, Prince Nduka Obaigbena’s 67th birthday, FCMB SheVentures and Shuttlers’ 10th anniversary. Speaking on the anniversary activities, the band’s Chief Operating Officer, Maria Tofowomo, said the late founder’s values remained central to its operations. “Our founder, Akiin Shuga, taught us that music is service to people, to God and joy itself. He advocated for a structured industry built on integrity, trust and professionalism, and our ability to sustain his legacy is a testament to those values,” she said. Also speaking, the band’s Business Manager, Jerry Odeh, appreciated stakeholders for their support over the past year, noting that the founder’s principles of service, excellence and professionalism continued to guide the organisation. He also disclosed that the activities of the Shuga Limb Foundation, a humanitarian initiative established by the late musician and anti-polio campaigner, had continued despite his death. As part of activities marking World Polio Day, the foundation recently empowered two physically challenged persons, providing one beneficiary with shoemaking equipment and another with a wheelchair to support their livelihood and mobility.
